page: Microsoft Azure E8s_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the ESv3 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 8 vCPUs (4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled), 64.0 GB of system memory yielding 8.0 GB per core, and a 131 GB local storage volume. The CPU is equipped with a 50 MB L3 cache, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512, AES, and FMA.

Benchmark evaluations indicate moderate memory and database capabilities alongside weaker raw compute performance. The server achieved average tier results in Passmark CPU tests, Passmark memory scores, and database operations, with Redis SET operations reaching 6.16 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth tests also placed in the average category, with read-only small block cached speeds at 365.1 GB/sec and uncached large block read speeds at 42.29 GB/sec. However, raw processing benchmarks like stress-ng single-core and multi-core, Geekbench single-core and multi-core, and static web serving throughput fell into the bottom 25% tier. LLM inference performance is limited, with text generation on a 7B model classified as poor.

From a resource density perspective, the E8s_v3 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for memory-bound workloads that do not demand intensive CPU performance. The inclusion of Premium Storage capability allows for high-throughput disk attachments. This virtual machine is best suited for relational databases, caching layers like Redis, memory-intensive data processing, and enterprise applications requiring a stable memory footprint without heavy computational overhead.
